prompt: Audit a 150uH 100kHz LT3757A candidate with 0.30 ohm shunt, typical 100mV sense limit and 0.70 efficiency sensitivity, 12V to 170V 2W. Check peak-current headroom and cold start into CCM.
review:
**Audit: LT3757A, 150 µH, 100 kHz, 12 V → 170 V @ 2 W, Rsense = 0.30 Ω**

## 1. Operating point
- Pout = 2 W, η ≈ 0.70 → Pin ≈ 2.86 W; Iin(avg) ≈ 238 mA at 12 V.
- Iout = 2 W / 170 V ≈ 11.8 mA.
- D ≈ 1 − 12/170 ≈ 0.929 (CCM); ΔI_L = Vin·D/(L·f) = 12·0.929/(150e-6·100e3) ≈ **0.74 A p-p**.
- CCM average inductor current = Iin ≈ 0.24 A → **peak ≈ 0.24 + 0.37 = 0.61 A**, valley ≈ −0.13 A (negative → actually DCM at this load, see below).

## 2. Peak-current headroom vs. 0.30 Ω shunt
- Typical sense threshold ≈ 100 mV → I_limit ≈ 100 mV / 0.30 Ω ≈ **333 mA** (typ). Datasheet tolerance on the sense threshold is significant (roughly ±10–20% typ-to-max depending on part/grade — **verify exact spec; I am not certain of the precise LT3757A limits**), so worst-case limit could be ~270–300 mA.
- Required peak in CCM at full load ≈ **0.61 A** → **~1.8–2.3× over the current limit.** This design cannot deliver 2 W in CCM with a 0.30 Ω shunt. The converter will current-limit and fold back well before 2 W.

**Verdict (headroom): FAIL.** For 2 W you need a sense resistor roughly 3–5× smaller (order 60–100 mΩ) to get ~0.9–1.5 A limit with margin, or accept lower power. Also check the LT3757A minimum on-time / max duty at 100 kHz for a 170 V output — high duty (0.93) with a boost controller is plausible but verify max duty and switch-node leakage/ringing.

## 3. CCM assumption and cold start
- At 2 W the ripple (0.74 A p-p) exceeds 2× the average input current (0.48 A), so the stage is actually **DCM at full load**, not CCM. True CCM (valley > 0) only occurs above roughly Pin > ~1.4 W-equivalent valley condition, i.e. heavier load than 2 W — so "CCM operation" at 2 W is a mischaracterization; it is boundary/DCM.
- **Cold start into CCM is the real hazard:** at startup Vout = 0, D ≈ 0, inductor current ramps with Vin/L, and the error amp demands max duty. With a 0.30 Ω shunt the 333 mA limit is hit quickly; the controller will limit peak current, but into a large output cap the startup is a series of current-limited pulses. Because the limit (~0.33 A) is *below* the steady-state CCM peak (0.61 A), the converter can **never reach regulation at 2 W** — it will sit in a current-limited hiccup/foldback state, and startup into the output cap will be slow and possibly stall below the UVLO/soft-start timeout depending on Cout.
- Additionally, at high duty the boost can have sub-harmonic/right-half-plane issues; with current-mode control and such a low current limit, loop behavior at startup should be simulated.

## 4. Bottom line
- **Peak-current headroom: insufficient** — ~0.33 A limit vs. ~0.61 A needed; design is over-current-limited at 2 W. **Change shunt to ≲0.06–0.10 Ω** (and re-check slope compensation, since high duty D>0.5 needs adequate slope comp with the new Rsense).
- **Cold start into CCM: will not complete** at 2 W as specified — it current-limits below the required peak, so it cannot charge to 170 V at full load; startup into Cout will be slow/stalled. Soft-start and Cout sizing must be checked, and the shunt/limit raised before claiming 2 W.
- **150 µH at 100 kHz** gives 0.74 A ripple — acceptable for DCM/boundary at 2 W, but verify inductor saturation > ~1 A and RMS rating; the ripple is large relative to average current.
- Efficiency 0.70 at 2 W from 12→170 V is optimistic-to-plausible but dominated by switching and gate drive at low power; confirm with measurement.

**Uncertainties:** exact LT3757A sense-threshold min/max, max duty limit, minimum on-time, and slope-compensation requirements are datasheet-dependent and I am not certain of the precise values — verify against the datasheet before finalizing. The efficiency figure and Cout value are assumed, not given.
